strengths: Clear problem identification: articulates a novel and well-motivated insight that existing image editing systems suffer from imbalanced division of responsibilities, with the generation module overburdened with design tasks

Substantial dataset contributions: DIM-T2I (14M images) and DIM-Edit (233K pairs) with thoughtful curation; demonstrates that real-world images with rich long-context annotations outperform filtered datasets

Strong empirical results: achieves SOTA/competitive performance on ImgEdit and GEdit-Bench-EN while being 10× smaller (generative params) than Step1X-Edit and UniWorld-V1; outperforms models with 7-14B parameters

Rigorous experimental validation: comprehensive ablation studies (Tables 7-8) isolating contributions of different data components and CoT elements; consistent evaluation methodology; robustness testing across different external designers

Reproducible and simple architecture: uses lightweight 2-layer MLP connector rather than complex designs, suggesting improvements stem from data quality; hyperparameters documented; promises to release datasets and models
Well-designed dataset creation pipeline: sophisticated DIM-Edit creation process with multi-stage quality assessment (misaligned/partially aligned/aligned) and structured 4-step CoT generation stages

Thorough evaluation across multiple benchmarks: GenEval, MJHQ-30K, ImgEdit, and GEdit-Bench-EN; visual comparisons clearly demonstrate advantages; fair baseline comparisons using consistent evaluation metric (GPT-4.1)
weaknesses: Critical practical limitation: model requires external designer (GPT-4o) during inference to generate CoT blueprints; cannot operate independently, adding computational cost and raising questions about whether improvements come from better data organization or leveraging a more capable external model

Limited architectural and methodological novelty: model is straightforward combination of frozen MLLM + trainable DiT + simple connector; primary contribution is dataset-centric rather than algorithmic innovation

Inadequately addressed data leakage concerns: DIM-Edit is derived from existing datasets (UltraEdit, ShareGPT-4o-Image, MagicBrush, SEED-Data-Edit-Part3); while distillation datasets excluded, potential overlap with evaluation benchmarks not thoroughly investigated; Janus-4o comparison provides incomplete assurance

Unvalidated DIM-T2I annotation quality: 14M images annotated by in-house models across 21 dimensions without human evaluation; no verification of annotation quality, coverage, or inter-annotator agreement; claims about 'broad coverage' lack empirical support

Performance gaps not fully resolved: underperforms Step1X-Edit on GEdit-Bench-EN (6.18 vs. 6.44); shows significant weakness on text-change tasks (2.34 vs. 7.72) due to missing training data, representing a notable blind spot for general editing

Incomplete failure analysis: limited discussion of when/why approach fails; no analysis of boundary conditions, sensitivity to poor CoT quality, or degradation with weak external guidance; ablations show what helps but not why

Unaddressed generalization questions: unclear how model performs with inconsistent or poor-quality CoT from external designer; zero-shot or human-provided CoT capability not demonstrated; robustness to different reasoning quality unexplored
Insufficient architectural justification: limited explanation for why 2-layer MLP suffices or why freezing Qwen2.5-VL-3B is optimal; no ablations on connector design choices or sensitivity analysis

T2I evaluation limitations: DIM-T2I contribution somewhat disconnected from editing focus; GenEval uses LLM-rewritten prompts which may diminish the value of long-context annotations; no direct analysis of how 21-dimensional annotations benefit T2I
Missing reproducibility details: computational cost and training time not discussed; inference latency with GPT-4o dependency not analyzed; details of 'in-house models' used for annotation vague

strengths: Well-motivated problem identification: Clear articulation of imbalanced responsibilities between understanding and generation modules with intuitive human workflow analogy
Strong empirical results: Achieves SOTA on ImgEdit (3.67), near-SOTA on GEdit-Bench (6.18 excluding text task), with 4.5× inference speedup over larger competitors despite using only 4.6B params
Comprehensive experimental validation: Thorough ablations (data composition, CoT components, initialization), multiple benchmarks, honest failure case disclosure, and self-play evaluation

High-quality dataset contributions: DIM-T2I with 21 thoughtfully-designed dimensions (14M pairs, 146.76 avg words); DIM-Edit with 83.4% ultra-high quality and 89% human preference over raw instructions
Robust generalization: Demonstrates compatibility with multiple external designers (GPT-4o, Qwen2.5-VL-7B, InternVL3.5-8B, GLM-4.1V-9B) showing approach is not model-specific
Strong reproducibility effort: Detailed data collection pipelines, quality assessment methodology, dimension specifications, and commitment to release dataset and models
weaknesses: Limited architectural novelty: Intentionally minimalist architecture (frozen MLLM + 2-layer MLP + trainable DiT) provides little methodological contribution; innovation is primarily data-centric rather than algorithmic

Inference design contradicts unified model claims: Requires external designer model at inference to generate CoT blueprints, adding computational overhead and external dependency; self-play variant (3.49) significantly underperforms main model (3.67)

Dataset reproducibility concerns: DIM-T2I relies on unspecified 'in-house models' with no detailed description; DIM-Edit entirely dependent on GPT-4o creating reproducibility barrier; dataset creation costs not discussed

Significant capability gaps: Text Change task performs 76% worse than Step1X-Edit (2.99 vs 7.40); acknowledged failures in complex text rendering, geometric shapes, and reference-free editing substantially limit practical applicability

Evaluation limitations: ImgEdit/GEdit-Bench-EN evaluation uses GPT-4 scoring potentially introducing bias; performance margins sometimes modest (12.6% improvement on ImgEdit); different experimental conditions across comparisons (VAE compression, proprietary data)

Insufficient CoT analysis: Limited investigation of why/what CoT captures beyond empirical validation; claim that CoT 'removes design responsibility' oversimplified since generation module still executes complex plans; no analysis of CoT quality distribution across task types
